Name: AI boom flywheel
Path: AI capability -> AI adoption and usage -> AI and cloud revenue -> Investor expectations -> Data center capex -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction -> Installed IT capacity -> National compute capacity
Story: Better models drive use and revenue, which validates investor belief, funds capex, and adds the compute that trains the next models. The engine of the build-out; long delays (permitting, construction, training) make it prone to overshoot.

Name: Scale and efficiency rebound
Path: Cost per unit of compute -> Reinvestment of efficiency gains in more computing -> Demand for compute -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction -> Installed IT capacity
Story: Scale and efficiency cut the cost of compute; cheaper compute is reinvested in larger models and more usage, so total electricity rises even as energy per operation falls (Jevons).

Name: Hub clustering
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Connectivity -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: Fibre, interconnection points and a supplier ecosystem make existing hubs more attractive, concentrating load and local impacts.

Name: Fiscal capture
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Local tax revenue -> Fiscal dependence on one industry -> Data center tax incentives -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: Tax revenue makes the host dependent on the industry, which sustains incentives and weakens appetite to restrict it, bringing more projects.

Name: Secrecy–distrust spiral
Path: Developer secrecy -> Trust in developers and officials -> Conflict and organised opposition
Story: NDAs and code-named projects erode trust; opposition grows; developers become more secretive to avoid it.

Name: Bring-your-own-power
Path: Peak load -> Interconnection queue -> Grid connection wait time -> Generation outside the public grid -> Power availability at site -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction -> Installed IT capacity
Story: Grid queues push developers to on-site gas turbines, which restores power availability and lets the build-out continue – moving emissions, noise and regulatory ambiguity to the fence line.

Name: Warming raises cooling load
Path: Electricity consumed -> Gas generation -> Operational CO2 -> Atmospheric greenhouse gas stock -> Climate change -> PUE
Story: Fossil-supplied load adds to warming; hotter ambient air raises cooling energy. Weak and slow globally, but locally visible in heat waves.

Name: Utility rate-base growth
Path: Utility grid investment -> Utility rate base -> Utility financial health
Story: Regulated utilities earn a return on capital, so large-load growth is an incentive to build – costs that ratepayers may carry if load does not materialise.

Name: Circular supply security
Path: Hardware purchases -> Hardware kept in use -> Hardware retirement -> Material recovery from retired hardware -> Secondary material supply -> Exposure to supply shocks -> Chip and equipment supply
Story: Recovering metals from retired servers lowers supply-shock exposure, easing hardware supply. Today this loop is weak because recovery rates for Ga, REE and other critical metals are low.

Name: Jobs promise
Path: Hope for jobs and renewal -> Public opinion -> Conflict and organised opposition -> Zoning limits and moratoria -> Land availability -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction -> Construction employment
Story: Construction jobs build hope and support, easing approvals for further projects. Can flip if operations jobs (few per MW) fall short of promises.

Name: Grid queue brake
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Peak load -> Interconnection queue -> Grid connection wait time -> Power availability at site -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: Load fills the interconnection queue; waits lengthen; sites lose power availability and the pipeline slows. The main physical brake on growth today.

Name: Power price brake
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Peak load -> Wholesale energy price -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: Rising wholesale prices make a region less attractive for new load.

Name: Ratepayer backlash
Path: Household electricity bills -> Large-load tariffs -> Share of grid costs carried by other customers
Story: Rising bills push regulators to large-load tariffs that shift grid costs back to data centers.

Name: Tariffs slow growth
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Peak load -> Utility grid investment -> Utility rate base -> Household electricity bills -> Large-load tariffs -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: The same ratepayer response also makes a region less attractive, slowing new projects.

Name: Neighbour pushback
Path: Installed IT capacity -> Continuous sound level -> Sleep -> Stress and anxiety -> Conflict and organised opposition -> Zoning limits and moratoria -> Land availability -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction
Story: Noise, light and disruption mobilise residents into opposition, leading to zoning limits and moratoria.

Name: Water scarcity shifts cooling
Path: Water lost to evaporation -> Municipal supply drawn -> Groundwater level -> Drought and water scarcity -> Evaporative cooling share
Story: Evaporative cooling draws down local water; scarcity pushes operators to dry or closed-loop cooling – which raises PUE and electricity use (problem shifting to the grid).

Name: Corporate clean procurement
Path: Clean energy procurement -> Renewable generation and storage -> Gas generation -> Operational CO2 -> Corporate climate targets
Story: Falling progress toward corporate targets triggers PPAs and clean firm deals. Strength depends on additionality and hourly matching.

Name: Public clean energy standards
Path: Operational CO2 -> State and national climate targets -> Clean energy standards -> Coal generation
Story: Missed state targets prompt clean energy standards that retire coal – if policy responds.

Name: Leverage limits capex
Path: Data center capex -> Debt and financial exposure -> Cost of capital
Story: Debt-financed build-out raises risk premia and the cost of capital, slowing further capex – the financial brake on overshoot.

Name: Mineral cost brake
Path: Hardware purchases -> Gallium -> Critical mineral prices -> Cost per unit of compute -> Reinvestment of efficiency gains in more computing -> Demand for compute -> Planned pipeline -> Capacity under construction -> Installed IT capacity
Story: Hardware demand tightens critical-mineral markets, raising compute costs and damping demand.

Name: Fab water constraint
Path: Hardware purchases -> Water embedded in hardware -> Drought and water scarcity -> Chip and equipment supply
Story: Chip fabs in water-stressed regions compete for water; droughts constrain chip supply.

Name: Disclosure rebuilds trust
Path: Conflict and organised opposition -> Disclosure rules -> Public availability of contract terms -> Trust in developers and officials
Story: Opposition wins disclosure rules; published contracts rebuild trust and dampen conflict.

Name: Security–transparency tension
Path: Developer secrecy -> Visibility of infrastructure and its labour -> Physical attack on facilities
Story: Attack risk justifies secrecy, which lowers visibility (and attack risk) – while feeding the R5 distrust spiral.

Name: Skilled-trades bottleneck
Path: Capacity under construction -> Construction employment -> Availability of skilled trades -> Installed IT capacity -> Connectivity -> Siting attractiveness -> Planned pipeline
Story: A construction boom drains electricians and linemen, slowing commissioning and, through it, the attraction of new projects. Also crowds out housing, grid and factory construction.
